letters.name: giyeok
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a gun — think 'g' for gun and 'g' for giyeok. It makes a soft g sound like in 'go' at the start of a syllable and a sharper k at the end.

letters.name: nieun
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like the curve of a nose — 'n' for nose and 'n' for nieun. It makes the same 'n' sound as in English 'nice'.

letters.name: digeut
letters.memoryTrick: Shaped like a door — think 'd' for door and 'd' for digeut. It sounds like a soft 'd' at the start of a syllable, but hardens to 't' at the end, like the 't' in 'hot'.

letters.name: rieul
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a rattlesnake — 'r' for rattlesnake and 'r' for rieul. It flaps the tongue like the Spanish single 'r' in 'pero', but at the end of a syllable it becomes an 'l' like in 'milk'.

letters.name: mieum
letters.memoryTrick: Shaped like a mouth — 'm' for mouth and 'm' for mieum. It's the exact same 'm' sound you make when humming 'mmm' with your lips closed.

letters.name: bieup
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a bucket — 'b' for bucket and 'b' for bieup. At the start of a word it's a soft 'b' like in 'baby'; at the end it becomes an unreleased 'p'.

letters.name: siot
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a summit or mountain peak — 's' for summit. It makes a crisp 's' like in 'sun', but when followed by an 'i' vowel it softens to a 'sh' sound.

letters.name: ieung
letters.memoryTrick: A perfect circle — like a zero, or an open mouth. At the start of a syllable it's silent (zero sound), but at the end it hums 'ng' like in 'sing'.

letters.name: jieut
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a jeep with a flat top — 'j' for jeep and 'j' for jieut. It's somewhere between an English 'j' and 'ch', like the 'j' in 'jeans' but with the tongue higher.

letters.name: chieut
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like jieut with a chimney on top — 'ch' for chimney and 'ch' for chieut. It's an aspirated 'ch' like in 'church', pushed out with a strong puff of air.

letters.name: kieuk
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a key — 'k' for key and 'k' for kieuk. It's an aspirated, breathy 'k' like the 'k' in 'kite', pushed out harder than giyeok.

letters.name: tieut
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like two teeth — 't' for teeth and 't' for tieut. It's a breathy, aspirated 't' like the 't' in 'top', stronger than digeut with a puff of air.

letters.name: pieup
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a pillar or part of a pipe — 'p' for pipe and 'p' for pieup. It's an aspirated 'p' like the 'p' in 'pop', with a strong puff of air, stronger than bieup.

letters.name: hieut
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like a person wearing a hat — 'h' for hat and 'h' for hieut. It makes the same breathy 'h' sound as in English 'hat', like a gentle sigh.

letters.name: ssanggiyeok
letters.memoryTrick: Double giyeok — 'ssang' means twin. Tense your throat like you're about to say 'k' but hold it tight, then release. It's a harder, tenser 'kk' than single giyeok, like the 'k' in 'sky' but sharper.

letters.name: ssangdigeut
letters.memoryTrick: Double digeut — the twin door. Tense your tongue against the roof of your mouth and release with no puff of air. It's a tight, tensed 'tt' like the 't' in 'stop' but held longer.

letters.name: ssangbieup
letters.memoryTrick: Double bieup — press your lips together tightly and pop them apart with no air. It's a tense 'pp' like saying 'p' in 'spot' but held tight, stronger than single bieup.

letters.name: ssangsiot
letters.memoryTrick: Double siot — the twin summit. Hiss like a snake but with a tenser, sharper sound. It's a strong, tight 'ss' like the 's' in 'see' but pushed through clenched teeth.

letters.name: ssangjieut
letters.memoryTrick: Double jieut — the twin jeep. It's a tense, pressed 'jj' sound, like forcing out a 'j' with your tongue pressed hard against the roof of your mouth, sharper than single jieut.

letters.name: a
letters.memoryTrick: A vertical line with a short arm pointing right — think 'ah' as in 'father'. It's a bright, open vowel like the 'a' in 'spa'.

letters.name: ya
letters.memoryTrick: Two short arms — double the arms, double the sound. Add a 'y' glide to 'a': it's 'ya' like the 'ya' in 'yacht'.

letters.name: eo
letters.memoryTrick: A vertical line with a short arm pointing left. Think 'uh' — like the 'u' in 'cup' or 'sun'. It's romanized as 'eo' but sounds more like a relaxed 'uh'.

letters.name: yeo
letters.memoryTrick: Two left-pointing arms — like 'eo' with a 'y' in front. Sounds like 'yuh', as if you're saying 'young' without the 'ng'.

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: A horizontal line with a short arm pointing up. Think 'oh' as in 'go' — a round, mid-back vowel. The arm points up, and your lips round upward too.

letters.name: yo
letters.memoryTrick: Two upward-pointing arms — like 'o' with a 'y' slide. Sounds like 'yo' as in 'yo-yo' or the greeting 'yo!'.

letters.name: u
letters.memoryTrick: A horizontal line with a short arm pointing down. Think 'oo' as in 'moon' — round your lips. The arm points down, like your jaw dropping slightly for this deep 'oo'.

letters.name: yu
letters.memoryTrick: Two downward-pointing arms — like 'u' with a 'y' in front. Sounds like 'you' in English, as if you're pointing at someone: 'you!'.

letters.name: eu
letters.memoryTrick: A single horizontal line — no arms. Keep your mouth almost closed, lips unrounded, and make a sound like 'euuuh'. There's no exact English equivalent; it's like the 'u' in Japanese 'sushi'.

letters.name: i
letters.memoryTrick: A single vertical line — like the letter 'I' in English. It makes the 'ee' sound as in 'tree' or 'see'. Simple and tall, just like the sound.

letters.name: ae
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅏ (a) and ㅣ (i) — say 'a' and slide toward 'e'. It sounds like the 'e' in 'bed' or 'pet', a bit more open than ㅔ.

letters.name: yae
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like ㅐ with an extra stroke — add a 'y' glide to 'ae'. It's 'yae' like 'yeah' but with a more open vowel. Rare but distinctive.

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅓ (eo) and ㅣ (i) — like 'eo' sliding into 'ee'. It sounds like the 'e' in 'bed' or 'set', very similar to ㅐ in modern Korean.

letters.name: ye
letters.memoryTrick: Looks like ㅔ with an extra stroke. Add a 'y' to 'e' — it's 'ye' like 'yes' without the 's'. Your tongue glides from the 'y' position into the 'e'.

letters.name: wa
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅗ (o) and ㅏ (a) — start with rounded lips for 'o' then open to 'a'. Sounds like 'wa' as in 'water' or 'waffle'.

letters.name: wae
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅗ (o) and ㅐ (ae) — round lips for 'o' then slide to 'ae'. Sounds like 'wae' as in the English word 'wet' but with a more open vowel.

letters.name: oe
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅗ (o) and ㅣ (i). Round your lips for 'o' and try to say 'e' — it comes out like the German 'ö' or the 'eu' in French 'peu'. Many Koreans now pronounce it like 'we'.

letters.name: wo
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅜ (u) and ㅓ (eo) — start with lips rounded for 'oo' then open to 'uh'. It's like saying 'won' in English, or the 'wo' in 'wonder'.

letters.name: we
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅜ (u) and ㅔ (e) — round lips for 'oo' then slide to 'e'. It's like the English 'we' or the 'we' in 'wet'. Used mainly in loanwords.

letters.name: wi
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅜ (u) and ㅣ (i) — round lips for 'oo' then slide to 'ee'. It's like 'we' in English, or the French 'oui'. Many Koreans now simply say 'i' for this vowel.

letters.name: ui
letters.memoryTrick: Combines ㅡ (eu) and ㅣ (i) — start with the flat 'eu' sound and slide into 'ee'. It's unique to Korean and sounds like 'eu-ee' gliding together quickly. At the start of a word it sounds like 'ui'; as a possessive marker it sounds like 'e'.
